methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia Beach schools bring ChatGPT under division oversight as AI use grows - 13newsnow.com
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Beach schools bringing ChatGPT under division oversight signals shallow, platform-mediated adoption—institutional guardrails around commercial AI tools rather than deep capability building, pointing toward distributed but surface-level integration.

signals.title: Norfolk could get AI assist for non-emergency calls - Yahoo
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk deploying AI for non-emergency dispatch represents municipal adoption of turnkey AI solutions—distributed geographically but shallow technically, as the city consumes rather than builds AI capability, reinforcing platform-dependent modernization.

signals.title: Emerald AI reaches unicorn status with $1.05B valuation - Virginia Business
signals.signal_reading: Emerald AI achieving unicorn status in NoVA deepens the concentration of AI capital, talent, and capability in the metro corridor—this $1.05B valuation represents the kind of deep technical capacity that remains stubbornly concentrated despite statewide digital ambitions.

signals.title: Parents call for less screen time, more intentional use of technology in schools
signals.signal_reading: Parent pushback against school technology in rural Southwest signals neither depth nor distribution—communities questioning tech adoption without evidence of meaningful capability building, reflecting resistance that could stall already-limited AI penetration in underserved regions.

signals.title: New proposal from grid operator PJM would require data centers to bring their own power
signals.signal_reading: PJM's proposal requiring data centers to bring their own power concentrates AI infrastructure burdens where data centers already cluster—NoVA's dominance in data center power politics reveals how physical infrastructure constraints reinforce rather than redistribute AI capability geography.
